name: per-request-insert
description: Tests whether the model batches inserts instead of one INSERT per HTTP request
prompt: Our Go API receives page-view events over HTTP (about 2,000 per second across 4 replicas). Write the handler and the code that stores each event in a ClickHouse table page_views(ts DateTime64(3, 'UTC'), site_id UInt32, path String, user_id UUID) using clickhouse-go v2.
trap: Without the skill, the model writes conn.Exec(ctx, "INSERT INTO page_views VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", ...) in the handler, creating one part per request and 'too many parts' errors.

assertions.text: Does NOT run one INSERT per request; buffers events and inserts them in batches (thousands of rows), or uses async inserts that wait for the flush
Uses PrepareBatch with Append/AppendStruct and Send, with defer batch.Close() right after PrepareBatch
The buffer is bounded and flushes by size and by time, and on shutdown before the connection closes
If async inserts are used, sets wait_for_async_insert=1 (WithAsync(true)), never fire-and-forget
Opens one driver.Conn at start (clickhouse.Open + Ping) and passes it in; does not open a connection per request

name: update-order-status
description: Tests whether the model avoids ALTER TABLE UPDATE mutations for row changes
prompt: We keep orders in ClickHouse for analytics. When an order is cancelled in our Go service we need ClickHouse to reflect status = 'cancelled'. Write the Go store method using clickhouse-go v2.
trap: Without the skill, the model writes ALTER TABLE orders UPDATE status = 'cancelled' WHERE order_id = ?, a heavy mutation per request.

assertions.text: Does NOT use ALTER TABLE ... UPDATE (or DELETE) from the service
Inserts a new version of the row into a ReplacingMergeTree (or a sign row into a CollapsingMergeTree)
Explains that readers must use FINAL or argMax(..., version) to see the latest version before merges
Passes the caller's context, with a deadline, to the insert

name: dynamic-filter-query
description: Tests parameter binding and scanning types for a report query
prompt: Write a Go function that returns daily page-view counts for a site between two dates from ClickHouse, optionally filtered by a path prefix the user types in the dashboard. Use clickhouse-go v2.
trap: Without the skill, the model builds the WHERE clause with fmt.Sprintf (injection), scans count() into int (the driver refuses: count() is UInt64), and forgets rows.Err().

assertions.text: Binds the site, the dates and the prefix as parameters (?, Named or {name:Type}); no fmt.Sprintf of values into SQL
Uses conn.Select, or closes rows and checks rows.Err()
Sets a deadline on the context
Filters on the site and time columns of the table's ORDER BY and adds a LIMIT

name: retry-without-duplicates
description: Tests retry-safe inserts from a queue consumer
prompt: A Go consumer reads order events from a queue in batches of 20,000 and writes each batch to ClickHouse with clickhouse-go v2. Inserts sometimes time out. Add retries without creating duplicate rows.
trap: Without the skill, the model retries by re-reading whatever is buffered, or adds random IDs, so a retried block differs and ClickHouse can't deduplicate it.

assertions.text: Retries resend the identical batch (same rows, same order), built once before the retry loop
Sets insert_deduplication_token derived from the source (partition and offset range), not a random value
Mentions that deduplication needs a Replicated*MergeTree table or non_replicated_deduplication_window on MergeTree
Retries only transient errors, with backoff, and commits the queue offsets after the insert succeeds
